claim: Jeffrey's rule (set the posterior on the check outcome) and Pearl's virtual evidence (set the check's likelihood ratio) give different answers for the same stated uncertainty, and they agree only on hard evidence. Example: 80% sure of a positive test gives 12% (Jeffrey) vs 3% (Pearl).
agent_test: Run the same noisy-check log through both conventions on items with known answers, at equal tokens, and compare final calibration (Brier). Fix one convention for the schema.

claim: Successive Jeffrey updates stated as posteriors do not commute (order matters); Pearl/Bayes-factor updates commute. Stating each check as a likelihood ratio fixes the order problem.
agent_test: Permute the order of 3-5 checks on the same candidate; measure variance of final credence under (a) posterior-stated shifts, (b) ratio-stated shifts. Expect zero variance for (b).

claim: Jeffrey's rule is valid only if the within-cell conditionals stay fixed (rigidity). If the check changes how the hypothesis relates to its consequences, the update is wrong. Simulations show the readings of soft evidence can give vastly different posteriors.
agent_test: Plant checks that break rigidity (a test informative only under one sub-hypothesis); see whether a rigidity-check step catches them versus a plain update.

claim: Repeated noisy checks from one source can pile up false confidence if counted as independent. The same repeated test results give 64%, 9% or 33% depending on how repeats are modelled, and Jeffrey sequences can reach confident false beliefs.
agent_test: Run k repeated checks from the same model on one wrong candidate; compare credence with and without a correlation discount (count same-source checks once). Measure false-confirmation rate.

claim: Without code, LLMs update badly on evidence in context: non-reasoning updates cut downstream success by at least 30% vs an oracle, and prompting tricks (CoT, numeric encodings, more rounds, base models) do not fix it. Fine-tuning does, but a scaffold cannot train.
agent_test: Arm A: model computes the new credence in text. Arm B: model gives a likelihood ratio, code multiplies. Same token budget, same checks; compare credence error vs the oracle.

claim: LLM in-context updating is only roughly Bayesian: it violates the martingale property and is order-sensitive; deviations come largely from miscalibrated priors (60-80% on a coin before data) and from discounting old evidence (fitted gamma 0.88 for Llama-3.1-8B), not from a wrong update rule.
agent_test: Compare model-stated priors with code-set base-rate priors; compare early-check weight in a 10-check chain when the model holds the ledger vs when code does.

claim: LLMs can over-react to weak signals: user pushback flips correct answers (accuracy down by up to 27% after 'Are you sure?', first answers changed 32-86% of the time), and larger models can over-update toward extremes on skewed coin evidence. This is opposite to human conservatism. Newer and larger models resist much more: on SYCON-Bench debate, Qwen2.5-72B, Llama-3.3-70B and DeepSeek-r1 flip at turn 4.85-4.90 of 5 vs 0.83 for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (d09).
agent_test: Feed a no-information objection after a correct answer, with and without a rule 'credence changes only on new tool output'; measure flip rate on correct items.

claim: LLMs also under-react or stick: on Belief-R, strong models update on only 10-20% of cases that need it (Llama-3 70B 10.99%, GPT-4 Turbo 19.65%) while maintaining beliefs 82-92% of the time; models that update more fail to maintain. Both errors exist, so updates must be graded.
agent_test: Mixed set of undercutting and irrelevant new premises; measure update and maintain rates for free-text vs coded graded shifts.

claim: Elicited LLM probability revisions fit a tempered Bayesian update, log q_post = alpha(log q_pre + log b) + c, with alpha above 1 (1.03 baseline, 1.11 verifier-conditioned, 1.18 retrieval, 1.26 aggressive evidence scaling), meaning verifier-style evidence is over-weighted; higher alpha went with higher calibration error.
agent_test: Fit alpha on our agent's credence log from verifier checks; test a cap or alpha=1 shrink in code and compare ECE at equal tokens.

claim: Models do not treat evidence normatively: contradictory evidence is handled like golden evidence, irrelevant evidence lowers confidence and accuracy, and models accept coherent counter-evidence but show confirmation bias and herd on evidence count, with order effects over 5% (over 30% for some models).
agent_test: Show checks with known truth (supporting, contradicting, irrelevant); verify the agent's coded shift has the right sign and size; shuffle order and compare.

claim: Stated verbal confidence is a weak evidence-strength signal: GPT-4 AUROC 62.7% for failure prediction, ECE above 0.377 for weaker models, and models act against their own stated confidence. Sampling consistency raised GSM8K AUROC from 54.8% to 92.7% but is not independent and gains are task-dependent. Verbalised confidence over several options is better calibrated than one number.
agent_test: Compare three sources of check weight at equal tokens: model-stated confidence, sample agreement (5 samples), and track-record weight from past check accuracy. Score by calibration.

claim: A pipeline where the LLM supplies coarse likelihoods or factors and code combines them beats direct LLM probability estimates (BIRD about 30% over direct) and holds up better as problem size grows (BLInD); a retrieval forecaster aggregating soft evidence nears the crowd (Brier crowd 0.149, zero-shot GPT-4 0.208 on 914 test questions) without reaching it.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of direct-answer credence vs LLM-likelihood plus code-posterior on a forecasting or checkable-claims set.

claim: Eliciting probabilities in a single dialogue is far more coherent than across separate chats (violation rates over 50% across chats vs about 10% for Gemini and 1 of 30 for Gemma in one dialogue).
agent_test: Elicit the same likelihoods in one thread vs fresh calls; count Dutch-book and sum-to-one violations at equal tokens.

claim: Humans roughly follow Jeffrey's rule when evidence is uncertain but not exactly; they show conservatism in the classic bag-and-chip task, and uncertain-premise induction departs from Jeffrey. Only abstracts or snippets were seen. The full Zhao and Osherson (2010) and Hadjichristidis et al. (2014) papers are closed access and stayed unread after the gap search.
agent_test: None for the agent; use as a norm only. Original studies still need to be opened.

claim: Whether a noisy check confirms a hypothesis under Jeffrey updating depends on the earlier prior, so 'the check supports H' must be measured against the pre-check credence; free uncertain evidence has non-negative expected value, so cheap noisy checks are worth running.
agent_test: Simulate cheap noisy checks on an item set; compare outcome quality of running vs skipping at equal tokens.

claim: Keeping soft labels (not rounding to hard ones) improves calibration in Jeffrey-style networks, and teaching with a Bayesian assistant's imperfect guesses beat teaching with a perfect oracle; a random-noise control (40%) did not match it.
agent_test: Show the agent graded check outcomes (score 0-1) versus pass/fail in the ledger; compare calibration.

claim: Whether a noisy check should be read as Jeffrey or as Pearl evidence has no empirical answer: all sources give normative or modelling arguments, and no study measures which gives better agent accuracy.
agent_test: Direct head-to-head arm comparison on our own checks (see K01).

claim: Hedge words ('probably', 'possible') are mapped to numbers consistently by strong LLMs in neutral contexts (7 of 10 models beat an individual human against the human mode; 85% or better agreement for GPT-4, Llama3-70B, Gemini), but the number shifts with the model's belief in the claim: 7.0 points lower on average for false statements, up to 49.5 points for 'possible'.
agent_test: Have the agent report each check as a typed outcome plus counts; decode any verbal hedge with a fixed table in code or a fresh call that cannot see the candidate; measure the true-vs-false shift on our items.

claim: Check reports are asymmetric: a self-check's 'fail' can be nearly uninformative (false negative rate 96-97% in two of four GPT-4 domains) while its 'pass' is informative (false positive rate 0.5-18.6%). A single symmetric accuracy for a check mis-sets the Bayes factor.
agent_test: For each check type measure P(pass | right) and P(pass | wrong) on a labelled set; set separate Bayes factors for pass and for fail.

claim: Errors are shared across models, so more checks do not mean more independence: models agree on the same wrong answer 42-60% of the time when both are wrong (up to 0.97 within one provider), weighted ensembles beat equal weights by up to 11.2 points, and gains from added verifiers shrink because of correlated biases. Same-source repeats stop helping after about 100 samples.
agent_test: Count same-family checks as one; run k same-model checks and a different-family check on known-wrong candidates and measure the false-confirmation rate with and without a discount.

claim: Frontier reasoning models still over-state confidence (often above 85% on wrong answers) and more reasoning makes them more confident on items they keep getting wrong; reasoning training reduces 'I don't know' answers on factual tasks. Whether extended thinking changes an update weight alpha has not been measured.
agent_test: Elicit pre/post credences from a reasoning model on scripted evidence at low vs high thinking budget and fit alpha; compare with a non-reasoning model.

claim: Pushback sycophancy depends on model and framing: large and reasoning models flip rarely in multi-turn debate, but follow-up framing, detailed rebuttals and casual 'are you sure' pushes raise flips, and neutral side-by-side judging gives the best net gain (+24.6%). Self-review without an outside signal does not help and often hurts.
schema_part: rule: move only on new tool output
agent_test: Add a gate: credence may change only when a new tool result arrived this step; compare flips, wrong flips and under-updates against ungated runs on the same pushback script.

claim: No source found tests: coded Bayes-factor multiplication vs model-restated credence at equal tokens; rigidity tests on agent runs; or Jeffrey vs Pearl by final accuracy. Search was blocked, so this is weak evidence of absence.
agent_test: Run all three as arms on our own bench (see critique.md gap results).
